title: Congruence of canonical strict-local maps at one admissible blowup
statement: Let (A,I) be a henselian pair with I finitely generated [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Let Ω be an algebraically closed field and let S be an AdmissibleCompletionPointSystem I Ω [def-per-admissible-completion-point-system]. For any index J of S and any n ≥ 1, write H_J = S.rings.obj J, H'_J = S.completedRings.obj J, b_J = S.base.app J and u_J = S.comparison.app J. Then the actual induced map H_J/(I^n).map b_J → H'_J/(((I^n).map b_J).map u_J) is bijective. These are the canonical pointed strict-local maps and structural maps specified by S, not arbitrary ring maps.

source.place: XX 2.4.4 proof, printed p.365; XX 4.4 final Note, printed p.374; Stacks algebra.tex, Tag 05WS (lemma-quotient-strict-henselization).

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-admissible-completion-fiber-iso] at the ideal of J and the integer n. The two geometric points factor through the infinitesimal fibres: S.closed and n≥1 give the first factorization, and S.comparison_point and the structural square give the second. The fibre isomorphism identifies their ordinary local rings and their chosen residue embeddings in Ω.

Identify the geometric strict-local rings with the algebraic pointed-etale colimits using [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-ring-triples] and [lem-sbc-etale-triples-localized-strict-henselization]. The map from each ordinary local ring to its fibre ring is the quotient by I^n, with kernel in the maximal ideal. Apply [lem-sbc-strict-henselization-surjective-quotient-core] to get their quotient strict henselizations. Use the same separable residue closure inside Ω and the universal pointed-colimit definition [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization] to identify these quotients.

The pointed uniqueness of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality] identifies the isomorphism just constructed with the reduction of the actual strict-local pullback. Transport by S.rings_obj, S.completedRings_obj, S.base_app and S.comparison_app. Thus the displayed quotient map is bijective; the statement does not merely assert existence of an unrelated ring equivalence.

theorem admissibleCompletion_strictLocal_congruence
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) [HenselianRing A I] (hI : I.FG)
    {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    (S : AdmissibleCompletionPointSystem I Ω) (J : AdmissibleBlowupIndex I)
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    Function.Bijective
      (Ideal.quotientMap (((I ^ n).map (S.base.app J).hom).map (S.comparison.app J).hom)
        (S.comparison.app J).hom Ideal.le_comap_map)
